test.name: Spec 0010 kern.bootsessionuuid differs after a reboot of this Mac

expected: after this Mac reboots, sysctl kern.bootsessionuuid differs from the value recorded before the reboot, so an observation from the old boot classifies as gone with reason boot_changed (spec 0010 AC-9, AC-11, Adapter macOS row Boot)
actual: after the reboot kern.bootsessionuuid is 4564385D-AE91-4FF6-A971-DDD132DA291C, different from 5E52ED28-4032-431E-9E64-B599BA083C49 before; the adapter reads the new value and the reconcile fixture classifies an old boot observation as gone with reason boot_changed
steps: The user rebooted this Mac on 2026-10-21 (local time, UTC+7); `sysctl -n kern.boottime` reads sec 1792537434, which is 2026-10-20T23:03:54Z.

Ran `sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid` after the reboot and compared it with the value the spike recorded before (record 01a14e57-f8c5-74d4-bf48-20f1fef1a381: 5E52ED28-4032-431E-9E64-B599BA083C49, boot at 2026-10-12 12:13:01).
Ran `cargo test -p stackly-platform-macos --test process the_boot_id_is_the_kernel_boot_session_uuid` on this boot: the adapter's boot id equals the sysctl value (1 passed).

Ran `cargo test -p stackly-core --test supervisor_start reconcile::a_new_boot` (a_new_boot_confirms_stopped_and_never_starts_the_instance): an observation whose boot id differs from the current one reconciles as gone with reason boot_changed, confirms stopped, and never starts the instance (1 passed). The unit test in crates/core/src/supervisor/classify.rs asserts GoneReason::BootChanged for the same case.

No instance was running before the reboot, so no registry held a real observation from the old boot; the boot_changed classification is proven by the fixture tests above on top of the native boot id change.
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (lead session, for ojiepermana, who did the reboot)
